intro: OpenAI moves to cut SpaceX's newly acquired Cursor off its models, and Anthropic steps into the gap; Google quietly relocates its Gemini safety team into its lobbying arm; Bitcoin's Fed-driven pullback deepens as its ETF inflow streak finally breaks.

items.headline: OpenAI moves to cut Cursor off its models after SpaceX acquisition
items.summary: OpenAI notified SpaceX it will wind down the contract giving Cursor access to OpenAI models, with a proposed shutoff date of November 12, saying it cannot trust SpaceX to honor its terms of service given Elon Musk's history of contract disputes. Anthropic co-founder Tom Brown said Anthropic will keep increasing Claude compute for Cursor instead.
items.why: OpenAI models made up only about 5% of Cursor's traffic, but the move turns model access into a competitive weapon right as SpaceX's AI arm and Anthropic jockey for position in coding tools.

items.headline: Claude Code patches symlink bugs that could bypass permission checks
items.summary: Anthropic shipped Claude Code 2.1.251, fixing bugs where file tools, plugin commands, Grep/Glob searches and the Workflow tool could follow symlinks to read or write outside approved locations after permission checks had already passed.
items.why: A concrete fix for the class of sandbox-escape bug that matters most as agentic coding tools get broader file-system access.

items.headline: Google moves its Gemini AI safety team into its lobbying division
items.summary: Google is relocating its roughly 90-person AI responsibility unit, which evaluates Gemini for chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear risks, from DeepMind to report to Kent Walker's global-affairs organization starting September 1. Several team members who sought transfers to stay inside DeepMind had those requests denied.
items.why: Placing the team that flags dangerous-capability findings inside the division that manages Google's relationships with regulators raises an obvious independence question.

items.headline: Z.ai releases GLM-5.3-Flash, a 320B open-weight model under MIT license
items.summary: Z.ai launched GLM-5.3-Flash, a natively multimodal 320-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 18 billion active parameters and a 1-million-token context window, publishing the weights on Hugging Face under the MIT license at roughly a tenth of its predecessor's price.
items.why: Day-one open weights scoring close to Claude Opus 4.8 on coding benchmarks keep pushing the price of capable models toward zero.

items.headline: OpenAI's first custom inference chip beats Nvidia's Blackwell in published benchmarks
items.summary: OpenAI and Broadcom showed the first benchmarks for Jalapeno, OpenAI's in-house inference chip, claiming 1.5x-1.9x more AI work per watt and up to 3.6x lower latency than Nvidia's Blackwell systems while drawing 700W versus 1,200-1,400W, with results partly verified on-site by SemiAnalysis on its public InferenceX benchmark.
items.why: The first credible outside evidence that a hyperscaler's custom silicon can beat Nvidia on inference efficiency, not just cost.

items.headline: VS Code 1.135 lets you continue Copilot or Claude agent sessions started elsewhere
items.summary: The release adds external agent sessions so developers can pick up Copilot or Claude Code runs started in other apps, an experimental 'Rubber Duck' feature that gets a second model's opinion on your work, and a streamlined agents window with per-model token usage breakdowns.
items.why: Microsoft is building VS Code into a control surface for multiple competing coding agents rather than betting on just one.

items.headline: Amazon to shut down Mechanical Turk and SageMaker Ground Truth on September 30
items.summary: Amazon confirmed it will close Mechanical Turk, the crowdsourced task marketplace it launched in 2005, along with SageMaker Ground Truth and Augmented AI, on September 30, ending Amazon's human-data-labeling infrastructure as newer AI-training-data startups have taken over the market.
items.why: The platform Bezos once called 'artificial artificial intelligence' outlasted the joke by two decades before AI itself made it redundant.

items.headline: Bitcoin extends slide to $77,678 as Fed rate-hike odds climb to 68%
items.summary: Bitcoin fell a further 3.3% to $77,678 on August 29, continuing Friday's drop from above $80,000, as markets kept repricing Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks, pushing the odds of a September rate hike to 68% from roughly 40% before the speech.
items.why: A second straight day of Fed-driven selling shows the rate-cut hopes behind bitcoin's summer rally are still unwinding.

items.headline: Spot Bitcoin ETFs post $202M outflow, ending nine-day inflow streak
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw $201.8 million in net outflows on Friday, breaking a nine-session run that had pulled in roughly $3 billion since August 17, with ARKB leading redemptions at $114.9 million while BlackRock's IBIT saw a comparatively modest $33.4 million withdrawn.
items.why: The first outflow day in two and a half weeks tests whether institutional demand can keep absorbing bitcoin's pullback.
